To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have introduced a new dynamic risk measure in an enlargement of filtration setup and that we have provided a representation result for it.

the BSDE approach to risk measures can be generalized to the case of an enlarged filtration and that the dynamic risk measure induced by the BSDE has a natural decomposition in two static risk measures, acting respectively before and after a given default time.
we introduce the notion of dynamic risk measure driven by a BSDE in enlargement of filtration framework and we characterize its main properties, providing also a robust representation formula.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dynamic risk measures induced in the context of a general enlargement of filtration.
dynamic risk measures in a general setting, where the filtration is enlarged by a random variable, that can be interpreted as a default time.
the study of risk measures induced by a BSDE in the setting of progressive enlargement of filtration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in a suitable enlargement of filtration framework, the robust representation of a dynamic risk measure induced by a BSDE is a pair of risk measure acting before and after a default time, and that the penalty term associated with the robust representation satisfies an inequality.
we have been able to extend the results obtained in a standard setting by Bouchard and Touzi (2004) to the enlargement of filtration framework.
the present work provides the first systematic study of BSDEs in the context of the progressive enlargement of filtration, with a particular emphasis on the dynamic risk measures induced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of enlargement of filtration, the dynamic entropic BSDE risk measures can be decomposed as a sum of two entropic BSDEs, one acting before the default time and the other one after it.

we provide a general framework for the study of dynamic risk measures in enlargement of filtration settings, where we are able to give a robust representation of the risk measure, a representation in terms of a pair of risk measure acting before and after the default time and we are able to study the dynamic entropic case.
we have extended the BSDE approach to dynamic risk measures to a more general setting, namely to the case of an enlarged filtration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the decomposition of the BSDE into two BSDEs, before and after $\zeta$, allows to decompose the risk measure into two risk measures, one on the pre-default filtration and the other on the post-default filtration.

the BSDE approach is a suitable tool for the study of risk measures in an enlargement of filtration setting and that it allows us to characterize the dynamic risk measure and to study its robust representation.

, in the context of defaultable markets, it is possible to define a dynamic risk measure which is robust to the occurrence of the default time and to its mark, and to characterize its properties in terms of the BSDE driver.
